operative_text.controlling:
2.26(1)  If a person who is served with a commencement
document, pleading or other document asks a lawyer or firm of
lawyers if the lawyer or firm is a lawyer of record in an action,
application or proceeding, the lawyer must respond to the question
in writing as soon as practicable.
(2)  If a lawyer or firm of lawyers whose name appears as a lawyer
of record in an action denies being the lawyer of record,
(a) every application and proceeding in the action is stayed,
and
(b) no further application, proceeding or step may be taken in
the action without the Court’s permission.

carrier_notes.BOOK_C: *[Alta. Reg. 124/2010, r. 2.26 effective November 1, 2010 (Alta. Gaz. August 14, 2010)]*

BOOK_A.title: Verifying Lawyer of Record
BOOK_A.related_provisions: 2.24 (lawyer of record; 2.29 (withdrawal of lawyer of record).
BOOK_A.commentary:
This Rule is of little use, as it could only expose pleadings not really ﬁled by the lawyer whose
name they bear, or ﬁled by a lawyer with a nonexistent client. The Rule has nothing to do with the
authority from the client to the solicitor.⁶
It is vital for the lawyer that he or she have express authority from the client before suing or
defending a suit or appealing. General authority to do legal work is not enough.⁷
If the client is
an artiﬁcial person, a resolution of its Board may be needed.⁸
If the corporation does not legally
exist at the time, any retainer agreement is void, there is no retainer, and the lawyer can recover

no fees from the corporation.¹
In urgent cases, the lawyer can ﬁle the pleading and then have the
client ratify the lawyer’s authority.²
If the plaintiff’s lawyer lacks or ceases to have authority, the
court may stay the suit.
A law ﬁrm acting for someone who uses another’s name in a suit without permission of the
person named, may have to pay costs personally.³
A judge strongly criticized a lawyer who
included in the applications which she brought, requests on behalf of the litigant’s named siblings.
She never swore that she had authority from any of the siblings, nor produced any evidence that
she had authority.⁴
One cannot open up a consent order, even before its entry, on the grounds of lack of authority
of counsel of record to consent.⁵
A lawyer becomes solicitor of record for a party by ﬁling some record in the action. The court
will not inquire into the solicitor’s authority without good reason, and a mere request by the
opposing party is not enough.⁶
The opposite party, or a shareholder in the company, can question the solicitor’s authority to
ﬁle proceedings for the company. And the lawyer will be made to pay the costs, even if he did
not know of the end of his authority, e. g. where the client died or, became mentally incompetent.⁷
Much the same is true if the client is, or goes into, receivership or bankruptcy.⁸
Where the newly-elected council of an Indian Band have instructed a lawyer to bring an
application in court and the resolution is in evidence in court, the court should not doubt the
authority of the lawyer, nor be deterred by evidence that some other members of the band
disagree with the litigation.⁹
A settlement of a suit under the Matrimonial Property Act is not binding if the formalities under
that Act are not followed.¹⁰
On authority of a solicitor to compromise a suit, see R.3.35n.
A party tried to upset a settlement made through her counsel (in her presence) by claiming
that her counsel’s performance had shortcomings, but the client did not waive privilege to let her
former counsel reply to that. In any event without ﬂagrant disloyalty or incompetence, the authority
of the counsel as agent would not be diminished.¹¹

A solicitor is presumed to have actual authority to consent to a partial settlement or to
arbitration.¹
The plaintiff was represented by a self-styled “Freeman” who, and whose organization, had in
the past shown themselves to be armed and violent in Manitoba, so the defendant’s lawyer was
allowed to appear using a pseudonym.²

footnotes.text: Quite similar to previous 1968 R.557(1), (3). It came from 1944 C. R.647 and ultimately from the Common Law Procedure Act 1852 s.7. Cf. (Imp. ) 2 Wm.4 c.39 s.17, Judic. Ord. s.10, and 1883 O.7 r.1.
See the C. P. E. , Chapter 4, Part K.2. Generally on solicitors’ authority, see the discussion and authorities in Hals. Laws of Canada, Civil Procedure, 333 ff. (1st ed.2008).
See the C. P. E. , Chapter 4, Part D; Lavallee Rackel v. R. (#2) 2000 ABCA 54, 255 AR 86, 93, 95 (¶’s 35-36), affd 2002 SCC 61, [2002] 3 SCR 209.
Obi Agbarakwe Pro. Corp. v. Condo. Corp. No.0726502 2011 ABQB 286, [2011] AR Uned 337 [but quaere as to the facts there].
See the C. P. E. , Chapter 4, Part K.4(c). Cf. R. v. Harrison [1977] 1 SCR 238, 8 NR 47.
See the C. P. E. , Chapter 4, Part K.3(b).

¶’s 67 ff. recite recent authorities on the need to use costs to restrain litigation misconduct, including costs against solicitors personally. The lawyer was directed to submit why she should not be personally liable for the costs awards: Re Sawridge Band Inter Vivos Settlement (1985 Sawridge Tr. ) v. Twinn and Pub. T’ee. (#__) 2017 ABQB 436, JCE 1103 14112 (Jul 12).

But an honest error (unknown to the lawyer consenting a second bill of costs had been signed and sent to the same ﬁrm), was enough to open up the unentered order, on condition of payment of $2, 000 for extra time to attend on the variation application: 1400467 Alta. v. Adderley (#2) 2013 ABQB 697[2014] AJ #1314.
Morin v. Trans Alta Utils. Corp.2017 ABQB 409, JCE 1403 06722 (Jun 27). See the C. P. E. , Chapter 4, Part K.3(b). But 2015 and 2016 English authority now questions this traditional proposition.
C. P. E. , Chapter 4, Part K.5.
Piikani N. v. Piikani Inv.2012 ABQB 719, [2012] AR Uned 861 (liquidator with limited powers).
Jang v. Jang 2000 ABQB 607, 272 AR 336. Cf. Smith v. Haworth 2003 ABQB 477, 345 AR 97.
Shannon v. Shannon 2023 ABCA 79, Calg 2101 0069 AC (Mar 6) (¶’s 40 ff. ).
